result.target_topic: Limitations of Remaining Performance Obligations as Forward-Looking Indicator
result.target_summary: Because the majority of Avago's revenue comes from contracts with a duration of one year or less, the disclosed remaining performance obligations are not indicative of revenue for future periods.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures address Remaining Performance Obligations under Note 3. The 2023 disclosure (D066) states obligations are not indicative of future revenue because customers generally do not exercise termination rights and most contracts are one year or less. The 2024 disclosure (D068) provides a similar caveat that obligations are not indicative of future revenue because the majority of revenue is from contracts with a duration of one year or less. They share the specific subject of the reliability of RPO disclosure based on contract duration/termination behavior.

comparisons.peer_topic: Remaining Performance Obligations Balance and Recognition
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose remaining performance obligations and explicitly address the limitation that short-duration contracts are excluded, making the disclosed figures less indicative of total future revenue. AVGO states that the majority of its revenue comes from contracts of one year or less, so its RPO is not indicative of future revenue. Similarly, AMD explicitly excludes revenue from contracts with an original expected duration of one year or less from its RPO disclosure, aligning on the scope limitation, though AMD provides a specific dollar amount ($85 million) for multi-year obligations while AVGO does not quantify the RPO in this specific disclosure.

sentences.text: In addition, the majority of our revenue is from contracts with a duration of one year or less.
Accordingly, our remaining performance obligations disclosed above are not indicative of revenue for future periods.

As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
The revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations does not include amounts which have an original expected duration of one year or less.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel recognizes net product revenue when performance obligations are satisfied via transfer of control, with substantially all revenue from product sales. Revenue is recognized at shipment or delivery based on shipping terms, even when products include interdependent software components accounted for as a combined performance obligation.
comparisons.comparison: The target disclosure focuses on the limitation of RPO as a forward-looking indicator due to short contract durations. Intel's disclosure focuses on the general criteria for revenue recognition (transfer of control) and notes that substantially all revenue is from product sales. While both deal with performance obligations, Intel does not disclose a specific RPO balance or discuss the limitation of RPO as an indicator in the same manner as AVGO; instead, it explains the timing of recognition (shipment/delivery) for its product-heavy business model.

comparisons.peer_topic: Revenue Recognition Policy and Contract Terms
comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue is recognized at a point in time when control transfers, primarily for short-term contracts at fixed prices, though some contracts have performance obligations extending beyond one year.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Micron discuss the prevalence of short-term contracts and how that impacts the visibility or nature of their performance obligations. AVGO states the majority of revenue is from contracts of one year or less. Micron confirms that substantially all contracts are short-term in duration at fixed, negotiated prices, though it also notes that from time to time, some contracts have performance obligations extending beyond one year, similar to AVGO's implicit reliance on multi-year contracts for any significant RPO disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Remaining performance obligations and revenue recognition timeline
comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024, consisting of contracted license, development, and hardware/software support arrangements. The company expects to recognize approximately 40% of this revenue over the next twelve months, with the remainder thereafter, excluding contracts with a length of one year or less.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose remaining performance obligations and explicitly exclude contracts with a duration of one year or less from this metric. AVGO states that because the majority of revenue is from contracts of one year or less, the RPO is not indicative of future revenue. NVDA similarly states that its RPO figure of $1.1 billion excludes revenue related to performance obligations for contracts with a length of one year or less, highlighting a common industry practice of excluding short-term contracts from this specific forward-looking indicator.
